label: Southern Patagonia fixed-coordinate contrast, PATICE 20 ka BP slice

location.coordinateMeaning: The same fixed point used in PATM-25000 and PATM-15000, preserving the world-coordinate comparison.

temporal.localTimeInput: 10:00 local hour, calendar day and season unspecified
temporal.supportedResolution: Published PATICE 20 ka reconstruction slice and point-in-polygon membership.
temporal.precisionBoundary: The slice supports ice-sheet membership and broad retreat context, not an exact annual ice surface, storm, snow state, or flow geometry.

habitation.evidence: The point remains inside reconstructed ice at 20 ka BP and predates the cited Southern Cone occupation horizon.
habitation.qualification: The card makes a local ice-interior claim, not a universal claim about all Patagonia.

viewpoint.support: Patagonian Ice Sheet surface at a point approximately 43.5 kilometres from the nearest reconstructed 20 ka margin.
invalidAlternatives: lateral moraine beside a valley glacier

visibleGroundTruth.claim: The point intersects the official PATICE Icesheet20ka reconstruction polygon.
visibleGroundTruth.visualConsequence: The comparison remains on ice at 20 ka BP even though the reconstructed margin has moved closer.

visibleGroundTruth.claim: The point is approximately 43.5 kilometres from the nearest reconstructed 20 ka margin in the source projection.
visibleGroundTruth.visualConsequence: The view is still an interior-ice composition, with any margin kept outside the visible claim unless a compatible sightline is separately established.

visibleGroundTruth.claim: The reconstruction supports regional change between slices while leaving local surface form unresolved.
visibleGroundTruth.visualConsequence: Temporal difference should arise from defensible ice-surface and atmospheric choices without inventing exposed land at the point.

obligations: Keep the fixed optic on ice.
Preserve the same coordinate, hour, medium, and frame geometry used at 25 ka.
Let the known closer margin influence only claims the sightline and source can support.
Treat exact surface relief, snow, and weather as bounded inference, using one ordinary surface mechanism and one depth or light relation to keep the image materially complete.
oracleOnlyContradictions: The 20 ka polygon still contains the point.
A deglaciated shore, soil foreground, forest, or open water at the optic is unsupported.
A visible margin is not guaranteed merely because its nearest mapped point is 43.5 kilometres away.
Exact local ice geometry is not encoded by polygon membership.

sources.title: The evolution of the Patagonian Ice Sheet from 35 ka to the present day
The arrival of Homo sapiens into the Southern Cone at 14,000 years ago

uncertainty: Exact 20 ka ice-surface elevation, slope, snow state, crevassing, weather, and season.
Whether the nearest reconstructed margin is visible from the chosen optic.
The reconstruction margin confidence is segment-specific; no confidence class is inferred for this interior point.
Calendar conversion uses BP relative to 1950 and is approximate at this visual scale.

review.notes: Point-in-polygon and nearest-margin calculations were recorded from the official PATICE version-2 reconstruction shapefiles.
